decisions.reason: As a low-carrying-cost software add-on tightly linked to the firm's core geospatial integration business and already presented as a stand-alone offer, it still has strong option value and little reason to be withdrawn so soon.

The digital twin service fits the firm's direction and market growth, but because it is more service-intensive and likely costlier to sustain than a software component, it faces a somewhat higher pruning risk while still being worth keeping as an option.

Authentication and identity delegation are relevant for enterprise integration, yet this offer is only close to rather than fully inside the core portfolio and may overlap with other identity-related options, so it is the most at risk but still not enough to justify immediate withdrawal.

An open GIS application development framework supports the firm's established custom-development and platform business, and as a reusable software foundation it likely has continuing option value at moderate carrying cost.

This identity and access service directly supports seamless integration of GeoIT applications into broader enterprise systems, so despite some overlap risk with adjacent identity offerings, the strategic fit favors keeping it on the market.
